history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Canonical references:
- ¬(A ∧ B) ≡ (¬A ∨ ¬B) and ¬(A ∨ B) ≡ (¬A ∧ ¬B) (De Morgan).
- (A → B) ≡ (¬A ∨ B).
- Contrapositive: (A → B) ≡ (¬B → ¬A).
- Negated implication: ¬(A → B) ≡ (A ∧ ¬B).
- For (¬A → B): rewrite antecedent implication gives (¬A → B) ≡ (A ∨ B). Comparing (A ∨ B) against (A ∨ ¬B) suggests a mismatch. Recommend Assistant to verify with a quick truth table check (focus on A=F rows).

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Quick truth check focusing on the suspected mismatch:
- (¬A → B) evaluates to T except when A=F and B=F (then F), because antecedent ¬A is T and B is F.
- (A ∨ ¬B) evaluates to F only when A=F and B=T; otherwise T.
Comparing:
- A=F, B=T: (¬A → B)=T vs (A ∨ ¬B)=F → mismatch.
- A=F, B=F: (¬A → B)=F vs (A ∨ ¬B)=T → mismatch.
All other pairs match.
Conclusion: The non-equivalent statement is (¬A → B) ↔ (A ∨ ¬B).
